quizzes.title: Unit 6 Assessment — Republic, Annexation, and War
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 6. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: The Constitution of the Republic of Texas (1836) divided the government into three branches. What were they?
Which group did the Constitution of 1836 leave out of citizenship?

answers.text: Settlers who came from the United States
American Indians and people of African descent

questions.text: What were "redbacks"?

answers.text: Uniforms worn by the Texas Rangers
Paper money printed by the Republic that quickly lost value because people did not trust it

questions.text: How did President Sam Houston try to deal with American Indian nations?

answers.text: He made peace treaties and met with their leaders.
He sent the army to force all of them out of Texas.
He asked Mexico to handle them.

questions.text: Which president moved the capital to Austin and set aside public land to pay for schools?
Who was the Tejano leader who signed the Texas Declaration of Independence, served in the Republic's Congress, and protected Tejano voting rights at the 1845 convention?
Under the Constitution of 1836, what did the president need before a treaty could take effect?

answers.text: The approval of two-thirds of the Senate

questions.text: What happened to Sam Houston's 1836 treaty with the Cherokee?

answers.text: It was approved and the Cherokee kept their land.
The Texas Senate refused to approve it, and the Cherokee were later forced out of Texas.

questions.text: What did President Anson Jones do in 1845 when Texas had two offers: join the United States, or peace and independence with Mexico?

answers.text: He chose for Texas without asking anyone.
He put both choices before the Texas Congress and a convention of delegates.
He asked Great Britain to decide.

questions.text: On what date did Texas become the 28th state of the United States?
What was the main cause of the U.S.-Mexican War?

answers.text: The United States and Mexico disagreed about the border: the Rio Grande or the Nueces River.
Mexico wanted to take back the Alamo.
Texas refused to join the United States.

questions.text: What does the Pledge to the Texas Flag mean when it calls Texas "one and indivisible"?

answers.text: Texas is united and cannot be split apart.
Texas will always be its own country.

quizzes.title: Unit 7 Assessment — Civil War, Reconstruction, and Juneteenth
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 7. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: According to the Texas secession convention's own written reasons in 1861, what was the main cause of Texas leaving the United States?

answers.text: A fight over the capital city

questions.text: What did Governor Sam Houston do in March 1861?

answers.text: He led Texas soldiers into battle in Virginia.
He refused to take an oath to the Confederacy and was removed from office.
He signed the order of secession.
He moved the capital to Galveston.

questions.text: The 1861 secession vote map shows that...

answers.text: most Texas counties voted to secede, but some, including counties in the Hill Country and North Texas, voted no.
every Texan voted the same way.
most Texas counties voted to stay in the United States.
only cities were allowed to vote.

questions.text: Why did goods like coffee, salt, and cloth run short in Texas during the war?

answers.text: Mexico refused to trade with Texas.
The goods were sent to the army in Mexico.

questions.text: Women running farms and businesses while men were away in the army is an example of what kind of effect?
Why did Colorado County print its own paper money in 1862?

answers.text: Coins and U.S. money were scarce during the war.
The county wanted to leave Texas.
Paper money was cheaper than food.

questions.text: Which battle near Brownsville in May 1865 was the last land battle of the Civil War?
What did General Orders No. 3 announce in Galveston on June 19, 1865?

answers.text: That Texas had won the Civil War
That all enslaved people in Texas were free
That the capital would move to Austin

questions.text: Why was freedom announced in Texas about two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation?

answers.text: Texas was far from Union armies, so the order could not be enforced until Union troops arrived in 1865.
The Emancipation Proclamation did not mention any states.

questions.text: What were the Black Codes passed by Texas lawmakers in 1866?

answers.text: Laws that gave Black Texans land
Laws that kept Black Texans from voting, holding office, or serving on juries
The words of General Orders No. 3

questions.text: Which of these happened during Reconstruction in Texas?

answers.text: Black Texans such as George T. Ruby and Matthew Gaines were elected to the Texas Senate.

questions.text: In what year did Texas become the first state to make Juneteenth an official holiday?

quizzes.title: Unit 8 Assessment — Cattle, Railroads, and the Changing Frontier
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 8. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: Why did Texans drive cattle north after the Civil War?

answers.text: Texas had run out of grass.
Cattle worth about $4 in Texas could sell for about $40 in the North.
The law required all cattle to be sold in Kansas.
Cattle could not live in Texas winters.

questions.text: What is a railhead?

answers.text: The front car of a train
A ranch house near the tracks
The end of a railroad line, where cattle were loaded onto trains

questions.text: Which leader opened a trail west to New Mexico with Oliver Loving and is said to have invented the chuck wagon?
Many of the first Texas cowboys learned their skills from...
The Kansas Pacific Railway printed a map calling its route "the best and shortest cattle trail from Texas." Why should a historian check this map against other evidence?

answers.text: The railroad wanted cattle business, so the map was trying to persuade.
The map was drawn by a cowboy.

questions.text: Which two changes helped end the long cattle drives by the late 1880s?

answers.text: Barbed-wire fences and railroads built in Texas

questions.text: How did the state of Texas encourage companies to build railroads after the Civil War?

answers.text: It banned wagons on public roads.
It gave railroad companies land for every mile of track they built.
It paid every passenger to ride.

questions.text: Which town was CREATED by a railroad company?
Look at this data: Dallas had about 3,000 people in 1870, 10,358 in 1880, and 38,067 in 1890. What does the data show?

answers.text: Dallas got smaller after the railroads arrived.
Dallas grew fastest after the railroads arrived in 1872 and 1873.

questions.text: Why were bison so important to the Comanche and Kiowa?

answers.text: They gave food, robes, tipi covers, and tools.
They were raised on ranches for sale.
They were only hunted for sport.

questions.text: Hornaday's 1889 map shows that...

answers.text: bison were spreading into new areas of Texas.
cattle trails ran through Palo Duro Canyon.
the land where bison lived shrank quickly, and the southern herd was gone by about the late 1870s.
railroads were built where bison lived.

questions.text: Which sentence is BALANCED?

answers.text: Nothing good came from settling the plains.
Ranchers gained grassland, while the Comanche lost the bison they depended on.
The plains were empty land waiting for settlers.

quizzes.title: Unit 9 Assessment — Oil, Depression, Dust Bowl, and World War II
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 9. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: What happened at Spindletop, near Beaumont, on January 10, 1901?

answers.text: A huge oil gusher blew in and started the Texas oil boom.
A dust storm buried the town.

questions.text: How did Pattillo Higgins show perseverance?

answers.text: He gave up when experts said he was wrong.
He kept believing there was oil under Spindletop Hill and searched for a driller after his wells failed.
He moved to California to find gold.
He built the first refinery in Port Arthur.

questions.text: Texas produced about 836,000 barrels of oil in 1900 and more than 18 million barrels in 1902. What does this data show?

answers.text: Oil production went down after Spindletop.
Oil production grew more than 20 times bigger in two years.

questions.text: Spindletop's own wells ran low by 1904. Why do historians still call Spindletop a turning point?

answers.text: Because the gusher photo was famous
Because the oil industry it started kept growing across Texas for decades
Because it ended the Great Depression

questions.text: Which sentence describes the LARGER oil boom, not just Pattillo Higgins?

answers.text: He formed the Gladys City company in 1892.
He placed ads looking for someone who could drill.
Hundreds of companies, refineries, and pipelines grew in Beaumont, Port Arthur, and Houston.
He noticed gas bubbling on Spindletop Hill.

questions.text: Which is an ECONOMIC cause of hard times in the 1930s?

answers.text: Cotton prices falling to about 5 cents a pound

questions.text: Why did soil blow away in the Texas Panhandle during the Dust Bowl?

answers.text: Native grass had been plowed up, and drought dried out the bare soil.
Too much rain fell on the fields.
Oil wells pushed the soil into the air.

questions.text: How did low crop prices make the Dust Bowl worse?

answers.text: Farmers stopped farming completely, so grass grew back.
Farmers plowed even more land to make up money, leaving more bare soil.
Low prices had no effect on the land.

questions.text: Dorothea Lange's 1937 photo of former Texas tenant farmers added what new cause to the crisis model?

answers.text: Tractors ("power farming") replaced tenant farm families.

questions.text: Which helped Texans recover from the Dust Bowl?

answers.text: Contour plowing, shelterbelts, and Civilian Conservation Corps jobs

questions.text: What was the "home front" during World War II?

answers.text: The people and work at home that supported the war
The front porch of the Alamo

questions.text: Which is ZOOM-OUT evidence about the whole state?

answers.text: Cleto Rodríguez sold newspapers as a boy.
Audie Murphy grew up in a sharecropping family.
More than 750,000 Texans served in uniform during World War II.

quizzes.title: Unit 10 Assessment — Modern Texas: Culture, Science, and Technology
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 10. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: What is culture?

answers.text: Only the food a group eats
The shared way of life of a group, including its music, art, food, language, and celebrations

questions.text: Lydia Mendoza was known as "La Alondra de la Frontera." What does that mean?
Which singer from Brownsville was called "the Queen of the Boleros"?
Jules Bledsoe of Waco is best known for...

answers.text: being the first to sing "Ol' Man River" in the Broadway musical Show Boat in 1927.

questions.text: Which sentence DESCRIBES a photograph instead of interpreting it?

answers.text: She was proud of her music.
She is holding a large guitar.
She was the best singer in Texas.

questions.text: Conjunto music mixes Mexican songs with an instrument brought to Texas by German, Czech, and Polish immigrants. Which instrument?
A strong museum label should include...

answers.text: the name and date, a detail, the community, and why it matters.
as many exclamation points as possible.

questions.text: What problem did Gail Borden's condensed milk solve?

answers.text: Fresh milk spoiled quickly, especially on long trips.
Surgeons could not keep blood moving.

questions.text: Why was barbed wire important on the Texas Plains?

answers.text: There was little wood for fences, and barbed wire was cheap and strong.
It carried messages like a telegraph.

questions.text: Michael DeBakey created his roller pump in 1932. About 20 years later, it became part of the heart-lung machine. What does this show?

answers.text: Inventions always matter the day they are created.
An invention may become historically important when it is adopted and changes lives, not only when it is created.

questions.text: Millie Hughes-Fulford, born in Mineral Wells, Texas, flew on the space shuttle Columbia in 1991 to study...

answers.text: how to build barbed wire in space
how the human body, including bones, changes in space

questions.text: Which is a NEW CONSEQUENCE of barbed wire in Texas?

answers.text: Fences closed the open range and led to fence-cutting fights in 1883.

quizzes.title: Unit 11 Assessment — Texas Government, Citizenship, and Economy
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 11. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: The Texas Constitution says, "All political power is inherent in the people." What does this mean?

answers.text: The governor holds all the power.
The government's power comes from the people of Texas.
Power comes from the federal government only.

questions.text: When did Texas voters approve the constitution Texas uses today?
Which branch of Texas government MAKES laws?
Who leads the executive branch of Texas and can sign or veto bills?
Someone says a new law breaks the Texas Constitution. Which branch decides?
Why does Texas divide government power among three branches?

answers.text: So laws can never be passed
So no single leader holds all the power, which protects people's rights
Because the Capitol has three wings
So the governor can make every decision

questions.text: Which of these must a person be to vote in Texas?

answers.text: A U.S. citizen, at least 18, a Texas resident, and registered

questions.text: Which action can a fourth grader take right now to participate in their community?

answers.text: Write a respectful letter to a city council member

questions.text: Adina De Zavala is remembered for...

answers.text: working to preserve the Alamo and other Texas historic places.

questions.text: Which comment at a public meeting shows respectful civil discourse?

answers.text: "Anyone who disagrees with me is silly."
"I disagree because the building is over 100 years old. Here is a photo from 1925."
Talking loudly while someone else is speaking
Leaving before anyone else can speak

questions.text: A dry summer means fewer tomatoes grow, but people still want to buy them. What usually happens to the price of tomatoes?
A company chooses to build a factory on the Gulf Coast instead of in the Panhandle. Giving up the Panhandle site, with its cheaper land, is the company's...

quizzes.title: Unit 12 Assessment — Texas Through Time Capstone
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 12. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: Which list puts these events in the correct order, from first to last?
In what year did Texas become a state of the United States?
What happened in Galveston on June 19, 1865?

answers.text: Freedom was announced to enslaved people in Texas (Juneteenth).

questions.text: "Ranching has been important in Texas from the Spanish missions to today." This statement describes...
"Texas went from part of Mexico, to an independent republic, to a U.S. state." This statement describes...
Which is the strongest caption for an exhibit?

answers.text: "The Lucas Gusher, Spindletop, 1901. It began the Texas oil boom, which changed where Texans worked."

questions.text: What does a bibliography tell a visitor?
Which test asks, "Does this evidence help answer MY question?"
Which source is a PRIMARY source?

answers.text: A website summary written this year
The 1883 railroad map printed by the Galveston News

questions.text: A visitor asks a question you cannot fully answer. What is the most honest response?

answers.text: Explain what your evidence shows and what you would still need to find out.

questions.text: Which shows courteous peer feedback?

answers.text: "I like how you used three units. One idea to make it stronger is to add a date to your second caption."

questions.text: Which of these is one of the seven pillars studied this year?
